alerts.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 25 at 2:21PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
ESFGJT

In the wake of today's precipitation, our attention will turn to the
Eastern Pacific. Tropical moisture is anticipated to spread across
the Desert Southwest early next week, drawing moisture from a pair of
Hurricanes; Odalys and Polo. The forecast becomes increasing complex
due to a closed low currently forecast to drive across the Southwest
CONUS as Hurricane Polo approaches the Baja California Peninsula.
Strong southerly winds ahead of the low are expected to pull tropical
moisture towards eastern Utah and western Colorado as early as Monday
morning. The challenge and uncertainty in our precipitation forecast
increase as the week progresses and the low traverses our southern
States. Excessive rainfall is most probable over AZ and NM, attm, but
the northerly extent poses a threat to our southern San Juan river
basins. Current forecasts suggests 1 to 3 inches of rain over Monday
morning through Wednesday. At face value, rivers and tributaries will
see a bump up due to said moisture. However, localized heavier
amounts could result in minor flooding across the southern San Juan
foothills and communities further downstream.

Rivers have responded rapidly to recent rainfall due to saturated
soils and increased runoff potential. Thus, prolonged periods of
additional rainfall over these regions would trigger a similar
response. The current precipitation forecast suggests larger peaks in
several creeks and rivers than what has been observed over the
previous 7 days. However, high end probabilistic rainfall amounts
(i.e. above 90th percentile) may lead to rivers exceeding action
stage to minor flooding. Most probable basins to see significant
rises include; the Rio Blanco, San Juan, Piedra, Los Pinos/Vallecito
Creek, and the Animas River Basins.

Convective storms and periods of heavy rainfall fed from said
tropical moisture could result in localized flooding impacts across
the CWA, however, confidence decreases rapidly north of the San
Juans. Please continue to monitor the forecast as these systems
evolve. Especially for those who reside and/or plan to recreate in
the southwest quadrant of the forecast area.

Cooler wet weather moves into the region Monday through mid week and dries out for the end of the week. Critical fire weather conditions are not expected. ...GUSTY E

alerts.description: Between CO 3 and Kirk Lane (1 mile east of the Durango area) from Mile Point 86 to Mile Point 92. Right lane closed due to paving operations. Starting Sunday at 7:01PM MDT until Monday, at about 7:00AM MDT. Full schedule below: • September 27, 7:01PM - September 28, 7:00AM Comment: Various eastbound and westbound single lane closures, reduced speed to 40 mph and up to 15-minute delays. For more information email: resurfacingproject@gmail.com.

alerts.title: Paving Operations-147652
alerts.description: Between Frontage Road and County Road 232 (near Durango) from Mile Point 88 to Mile Point 89.5. Paving operations. Starting Sunday at 7:00PM MDT until Monday, at about 7:00AM MDT. Full schedule below: • September 27, 7:00PM - September 28, 7:00AM Comment: The US 550-US 160 Grandview Interchange exit and entrance ramps will experience staggered nighttime closures from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m., Sunday night through Friday morning. Detour: motorists traveling southbound and northbound on US 550 between Durango and New Mexico will detour on Wilson Gulch Drive and Three Springs Boulevard to access the Grandview Bridge and points beyond. For more information email: resurfacingproject@gmail.com.

alerts.title: US 160 Pagosa Springs Reconstruction-147577
alerts.description: Between US 84 and Pike Drive (Pagosa Springs) from Mile Point 144.3 to Mile Point 141.8. Road construction. Starting September 28, 2026 at 7:00AM MDT until September 28, 2026 at about 6:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • September 28, 7:00AM - September 28, 6:00PM Comment: Harman Park & Piedra Road-Work is underway at this intersection of US 160. Working hours will be intermittent day and night so motorists should plan for potential delays, Monday-Saturday. Please allow extra time to get through the work zone. Safety benefits of this work includes pedestrian safety upgrades and ADA accessibility improvements. Expect lane shifts and up to 15-minute delays. Crews will switch two-way traffic into the eastbound lanes, perform temporary striping operations and begin asphalt milling in the westbound lanes. Parking will not be permitted on US 160 and vehicles will be towed at the owner's expense. Westbound lane closures, 10’ width and 75’ length restrictions will remain in place 24/7 through end of 2026. Work is weather-dependent. For questions contact the project team at 970-335-9230 or Pagosa160reconstruction@gmail.com Project Webpage: www.codot.gov/projects/us160pagosasprings
